title: performance canary: automated latency/throughput regression detector and rollout guards
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Our perf canary currently requires manual threshold tuning and manual promotion decisions. This causes slow detection of regressions and occasional noisy rollouts. This PR introduces an automated detection pipeline that evaluates canary-specific latency and throughput signals, applies hysteresis and KV-cache-aware thresholds, and enforces rollout guards to block promotions when regressions are detected. Scope: detector service + metrics exporter + rollout-controller changes + tests + docs. Key behaviors: 1) continuous evaluation of P95/P99 latency and per-model throughput deltas over sliding windows, 2) model- and route-aware baselines that account for sequence-length distribution and batching, 3) hysteresis to avoid flapping (configurable window and sensitivity), 4) KV-cache-aware adjustments so small KV-hit regressions don't trigger false positives, 5) automatic rollback/pause and canary-failure alerts with links to the canary dashboard. Checklist: - [x] detector service implementation - [x] rollout controller integration - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf canary e2e tests in perf-lab - [x] docs + runbook updates - [x] Linear/Jira links included. This is intended for immediate rollout to Dedicated and Hosted canaries; default sensitivity is conservative and can be tuned per-customer. See release_notes for helpful summary.

review_comments: Evan Chen: Nice work, Priya. A few questions: how does baseline bootstrap for new models with little traffic? Can we avoid noisy baselines during rampups?
Priya Nair: Answered: detector uses an exponential warmup and fallback to historical cohort baselines; added config docs and tests for ramp-up behavior.
Sofia Patel: Requested change: add a KV-hit adjustment toggle per-route (we have customers who want strict latency thresholds).
Priya Nair: Added per-route toggle and updated rollout-controller to respect route overrides; added unit tests.
Alex Morgan: CI flaked on the perf-lab test once — saw a timeout on the first run. Can you make the test tolerant to transient infra noise?
Priya Nair: Adjusted test to retry short-lived infra flakiness and added a failure-mode fixture; reran CI and tests passed.
Evan Chen: Approving after small nits fixed (naming + one log level change).

release_notes: Added an automated performance canary detector that enforces rollout guards on latency and throughput regressions. Default sensitivity is conservative; operators can tune per-model and per-route hysteresis and KV-cache adjustments. Includes new canary_kv_adjusted_p95 metric, rollout-block alerts, runbook updates, and e2e perf tests.
notes_for_oncall: If a canary is blocked, the rollout-controller will emit 'canary-regression-detected' alert with a link to the canary dashboard. First steps: check canary_kv_adjusted_p95 and canary_throughput_delta metrics, review baseline cohort, and validate KV-hit rate; rollbacks are automatic but you can manually unpause after root-cause fix.
